title: Build a shared setgid directory
goal: Combine group access and setgid inheritance without exposing files to outsiders.
challenge: Create locked ll-u5a/ll-u5b, disposable group ll-u5team and /srv/ll-u5. Team members must create and edit each other's small notes; nobody must be denied. Verify inherited group and permissions independently. No credentials or sudo rights for lab accounts.

steps.command: ! getent passwd ll-u5a && ! getent passwd ll-u5b && ! getent group ll-u5a && ! getent group ll-u5b && ! getent group ll-u5team && test ! -e /home/ll-u5a && test ! -e /home/ll-u5b && test ! -e /srv/ll-u5 && sudo groupadd ll-u5team && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash -G ll-u5team ll-u5a && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash -G ll-u5team ll-u5b
steps.explanation: Guard all fixture identities and paths before setup. Both accounts remain password locked.
steps.expected: Two team members with separate primary groups.

steps.explanation: 2 sets directory setgid: new children inherit the directory group. Group rwx allows creation/traversal.

steps.command: sudo runuser -u ll-u5a -- bash -c 'umask 0007; printf "first\n" > /srv/ll-u5/note.txt; mkdir /srv/ll-u5/sub'
steps.explanation: A process-local mask allows group write, not other access. Setgid does not itself grant file read/write.
steps.expected: note inherits team group and 660; subdirectory inherits setgid and 2770.

steps.explanation: Cross-user writing must really work; a listing alone is not proof.
steps.expected: first and second, written by two different users.

steps.command: sudo stat -c '%U:%G %a' /srv/ll-u5/note.txt /srv/ll-u5/sub; sudo runuser -u nobody -- ls /srv/ll-u5
steps.explanation: Check inheritance and outsider denial separately. A shared writable directory allows members to remove names; setgid does not prevent that.
steps.expected: Team group on both children, no execute on note; nobody denied.

hints: chmod 0777 would admit outsiders; retain other=0.
Without setgid, a newly created file usually gets the creator's primary group.
A restrictive umask can defeat group-write even when setgid inheritance is correct.
review: Actual ll-u5b append/read of ll-u5a file, inherited team group, 660/2770 children, outsider denied.
Explain shared-directory deletion rights; sticky-bit policy is not configured here.
coverage: LPIC-1 104.5 setgid directories, group ownership; 107.1 reinforcement. Partial coverage; original material, self-review only. No automatic assessment or full LPIC preparation.
